stem: Which of the following is an immunisation error-related adverse event following immunisation (AEFI)?

options.text: A coincidental heart attack shortly after vaccination
Administering a live vaccine to an immunocompromised patient
Extensive limb swelling after DTP vaccination
An ulcer at the BCG vaccination site

explanation: Immunisation error-related AEFI is the correct concept. It occurs when an adverse event results from a preventable error in vaccine selection, storage, preparation, or administration, such as giving a live vaccine to an immunocompromised patient.
rationale: This category refers to harm caused by a mistake in the immunisation process rather than the vaccine itself or an unrelated coincidental event.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a heart attack occurring after vaccination but not caused by it is a coincidental event.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because giving a live vaccine to an immunocompromised patient is a preventable administration error involving a contraindication.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because extensive limb swelling after DTP vaccination is a vaccine product-related reaction.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because an ulcer at the BCG site is an expected vaccine-specific local reaction.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because fainting immediately after vaccination is a stress-related or coincidental reaction, not an immunisation error-related AEFI.

source.hint: Focus on an event caused by a mistake in the decision-making or administration process by the healthcare provider.
